**Yes, a 20,000 mAh power bank is generally fine in your carry-on, but not in checked luggage.**

**Why it's allowed:** The FAA limits spare lithium-ion batteries and power banks to 100 Wh each. Most 20,000 mAh banks come in around 74 Wh, well under that. To check yours, multiply volts by amp-hours (20,000 mAh = 20 Ah; at a typical 3.7 V, that's about 74 Wh). Many banks print the Wh rating on the case. ([FAA: Airline Passengers and Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries))

**Rules to follow:**
- **Carry-on only.** Spare batteries and power banks are prohibited in checked bags. If your carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you in the cabin. ([FAA: Lithium Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- **Protect the terminals.** Keep it in its retail packaging, a pouch, or a case, or tape over the ports so nothing metal can short them. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- **Don't bring a damaged or recalled unit.** Swollen, damaged, or recalled batteries aren't allowed in carry-on or checked bags. ([FAA: PackSafe](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe?packsafeq=power+bank))
- **Check your airline's policy.** The FAA notes that many airlines set stricter limits, including on how many power banks you can carry. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries))
- **Tell the crew right away** if the bank gets hot, swells, or smokes in flight. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
